title: El cuarto
goal: Rent a room by the month instead of the night
culture: You rent from a woman who lives in the same house. There is no agency, no contract and nothing to sign — the agreement is the two of you saying the numbers out loud. Which is why the water and the light have to be asked about now, by you.

beats.es: Buenas. Sí, tengo un cuarto desocupado. ¿Lo quiere ver?
beats.objective: Ask to take it by the month
beats.en: Would you rent it to me by the month?
beats.good: Por mes, not por noche. The hostel was fifteen dollars a night; this is a different arrangement and this is the sentence that opens it.

beats.es: Claro. Son cien dólares el mes.
beats.good: El alquiler is the rent. Say the number back out loud: there is nothing to sign, so the two of you agreeing out loud IS the agreement.

beats.objective: Ask whether the water is included
beats.good: Ask, because often it is not, and the water and the light are what turn a cheap room into an expensive one.

beats.es: El agua sí. La luz la paga usted aparte.
beats.good: ¿Desde cuándo? asks when it starts. Everything here is agreed by talking, so the date has to be said out loud as well.
